title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Great engineering earns a place on the watchlist; only an asymmetric entry price earns fresh capital.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC Mechatronics Ltd (NSE: SEDEMAC) is an IIT Bombay-incubated (2007) powertrain electronics firm [2]. It builds patented sensorless Integrated Starter Generators (ISG), EFI ECUs, EV motor controllers (ISAAC), and genset AMF controllers [7, 8, 9]. On our price-blind audit (Chapters 1–6), SEDEMAC earns a COMPOUNDER_PASS (`kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH`). Revenue compounded at 34.5% over five years to ₹1,058 Cr in FY26 (₹1,265 Cr TTM), with 35.3% ROCE and 26.9% ROE [1]. Mobility drives 86.2% of FY26 sales (₹912 Cr), while Industrial genset controls add 13.8% (₹146 Cr) with ~75% Indian AMF share [4, 8].

In Pass 2 (Chapters 7–9), we test this business against its market price. At the November 13, 2026 close of ₹3,129.10 (Market Cap ₹13,837 Cr), the stock trades +131.4% above its March 2026 IPO price of ₹1,352 [1, 18, 22]. It commands 107.0x trailing P/E and 26.5x P/B [1, 22]. Our Reverse DCF shows the market prices in ~28% annual revenue growth for ten years. Our 12-month Base fair value is ₹3,050 (-2.5% vs CMP). FY26 Free Cash Flow was -₹47 Cr, Debtor Days rose to 46.1, and Sep 2026 debt surged 5x to ₹352 Cr for MF3/MF5 capex and chip inventory [1, 5]. Therefore, new capital is REJECTED (`VALUATION`, `CASH_FLOW`).

For our existing Zerodha holding, the portfolio decision is distinct from new-capital rejection. Zerodha holds 200 shares at ₹2,025.49 average cost (₹4,05,098.25 total), now worth ₹6,25,820.00 (+54.49% gain). At 14.56% of the Indian account, SEDEMAC is our largest single equity position. Weekly structure holds above the 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91), though the daily 50-DMA (₹3,138.55) is flat-to-falling with 8 distribution days. We recommend TRIM_OVERWEIGHT: sell 100 shares (~₹3,12,910) to cut weight in half to ~7.28% and hold 100 core shares behind a ₹2,696.82 hard stop.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional monograph on SEDEMAC Mechatronics Ltd. Before we walk through the ten chapters together, let me lay out the exact architecture of our decision—because this is one of the clearest examples you will ever encounter of why we separate business underwriting from stock-price judgment.

In Pass 1, working completely blind to the share price, we examined SEDEMAC's origin inside IIT Bombay in 2007, its patented sensorless motor-control algorithms, its dominant ~75% share in Indian genset AMF controllers, and its rapid scaling inside TVS Motor's two-wheeler lineup. The business earned an unambiguous COMPOUNDER_PASS: 34.5% five-year revenue growth to ₹1,058 Cr, 35.3% ROCE, and genuine engineering IP. At the same time, our forensic audit flagged three real risks: 75% to 81% customer concentration in TVS Motor, negative FY26 Free Cash Flow of -₹47 Cr, and a nearly fivefold jump in borrowings to ₹352 Cr in September 2026 to fund MF3, Shoolagiri (MF5), and semiconductor inventory.

In Pass 2, we reviewed the November 13, 2026 NSE close of ₹3,129.10. At 107.0 times trailing earnings (₹13,837 Cr market cap), the stock has more than doubled since its March 2026 IPO at ₹1,352 and already discounts nearly 28% annual compounding for the next decade. Even on a pullback to its ₹3,070–₹3,176 support band, our ₹3,050 Base Case fair value offers negative reward-to-risk. Accordingly, we **REJECT** new capital across all horizons.

Yet because Zerodha currently holds 200 shares at ₹2,025.49 cost—worth ₹6,25,820 (+54.49%) and representing an outsized 14.56% of our Indian portfolio—our holding action is **TRIM_OVERWEIGHT**. We trim 100 shares (~₹3,12,910) to cut concentration in half to ~7.28% (redeploying 70% to Cash and 30% to Stage 2 shortlist name MANORAMA) while keeping 100 core shares behind a hard ₹2,696.82 stop.

As we walk through Chapters 1 to 9, keep this dual lens in mind: admire the engineering in Pune, respect the Stage 2 institutional accumulation on the tape, and let valuation and position-sizing math protect your capital.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a holding grows to 14.56% of your portfolio at 107x trailing earnings with 75–81% single-customer exposure, trimming 35% of the position is not a lack of conviction—it is portfolio craftsmanship.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Dual-Edition Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 were written strictly price-blind—without checking a single ticker quote, P/E multiple, or portfolio holding—so you can judge the factory, the patents, the distribution network, and the cash-flow statements on their own merits. Chapters 7 through 9 then test that business reality against Reverse DCF math, Stan Weinstein Stage 2 structure, and our live Zerodha portfolio weights.

In Chapter 1, we trace SEDEMAC's origin from Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan's IIT Bombay lab in 2007 through its early venture backing and March 2026 IPO. Chapter 2 dissects the Mobility (86.2%) and Industrial (13.8%) segments with concrete real-world OEM examples—from TVS Jupiter sensorless ISG to Kirloskar and Generac CPCB IV+ genset controllers. Chapter 3 maps the B2B OEM engineering co-development model and walks through a deterministic ₹100 FY26 revenue-to-FCF waterfall.

Chapter 4 weighs the sensorless patent moat against Bosch, Denso, and Deep Sea Electronics alongside a clickable External Learning Hub. Chapter 5 audits six leading operational KPIs and management's execution record, while Chapter 6 conducts 6-year financial forensics—highlighting the H1 FY27 borrowings surge (₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr), Debtor Days stretch (24 to 46.1), and negative FY26 FCF (-₹47 Cr). Finally, Chapters 7, 8, and 9 bring valuation, technicals, and our 200-share Zerodha position together into an executable, unhedged action plan.

Keep one overarching lesson in mind as you read: an institutional investor never confuses a great company with a great stock at any price. SEDEMAC's patented sensorless motor-control architecture, 35.3% ROCE, and ~75% Indian genset AMF share make it one of the most technically impressive mid-caps to list on the NSE in 2026. Yet at ₹3,129.10 and 107.0x trailing earnings, the market has already pulled forward years of execution—making position sizing, overweight trimming, and strict stop-loss discipline essential.

That is why our verdict is intentionally split across new capital and existing holdings. If you are sitting on fresh cash today, you do not chase a 107x P/E stock with negative FY26 Free Cash Flow and 75–81% single-customer reliance—you reject it and deploy into higher-asymmetry Stage 2 setups like MANORAMA or hold cash. If you already hold 200 shares from ₹2,025.49, you respect the weekly 30W SMA trend while cutting portfolio weight in half from 14.56% to 7.28% by selling 100 shares and protecting the remaining 100 shares behind a hard ₹2,696.82 stop.

Finally, remember that every number in this monograph—from the ₹100 revenue-to-FCF waterfall in Chapter 3 to the Reverse DCF and peer table in Chapter 7 and the Stage 2 VCP ledger in Chapter 8—is anchored to audited FY26/H1 FY27 filings and the verified November 13, 2026 NSE market close. Nothing is extrapolated from memory, and no conclusion is hedged. Every table, scenario target, and portfolio alert reconciles cleanly back to our primary evidence pack, ensuring full transparency. Let us begin in Chapter 1 with the 2007 IIT Bombay lab where SEDEMAC's sensorless control story started.
